title: Lamps on the Water
logline: Lamps are lit on still water at dusk and a crew works the same patient rhythm all night, not knowing until dawn whether the night was worth it.
human_question: What does a whole night of patient, repeated effort feel like when the result is still not known?

situation.what_happens: A crew that fishes by light goes out at dusk, sets its lamps, and works a rhythm that does not change for eight or nine hours. Insects and fish gather to the light. Nothing about the night tells the crew how it is going until it is nearly over. At dawn the catch is counted and it is either a night that pays or a night that does not, and either way the same night happens again tomorrow.
situation.who_is_involved: The crew who work the lamps through the night; the households the night's takings belong to; whoever buys the catch at first light and sets its price.
situation.what_is_at_stake: One night's income against one night's fuel, lamps and sleep, repeated across a season in which the good nights have to pay for the bad ones.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins at dusk and it ends at dawn, and it is the same every time except for the amount at the end. The pressures are weather, fuel cost and the accumulation of nights that did not pay. It ends in a catch or in very little, and reality decides which.

concept_merge.why_together: No merge survives inspection, which is why this idea is dropped rather than repaired. The two links it carried were both supporting and neither held: a night's uncertain livelihood was read as an occasion for aversion although no aversion is claimed or observed anywhere in the situation, and a crew's steady, unbroken all-night rhythm was offered as an image of restlessness, which inverts the concept, since restlessness is agitation that will not settle on its object [C022-P:L31] and sustained attention is the opposite of it. The one thing in the digests this situation genuinely sits on is the compendium's image of the moth flying into the lamp flame because the flame looks pleasant [C022-P:L67], and the digest's own note on that image says in as many words that the crew must never be framed as the moths.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Nothing this group needs that another film does not already carry better. The group's account of uncertainty and its account of unsettledness are both held live by kept ideas, with grounds the digests actually support.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Nothing is claimed. The concept links this idea carried were withdrawn rather than rewritten, so it makes no teaching claim at all in this state.
what_must_be_real: If the idea were ever restored, the crew, their methods and their night's catch would have to be entirely genuine and unscripted, and no reading of the source's lamp-and-moth image could be laid over the people working the lamps.
position_hint: none: the idea is dropped, and nothing in the group's arc depends on it. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Turning a livelihood into a visual allegory that frames the crew as the moths, which the digest forbids by name.
Reading sustained, patient attention as the restlessness the sources describe, which reverses the concept.
Long night material with no human stake and no supported concept underneath it.
drop_if: Already dropped: no concept link in the group's four digests supports the situation as it stands.

connections.note: Two night vigils; only one of them has a state of mind in it that the sources actually describe.

selection.reason: Both its links failed the digests: the aversion link was loose, and the restlessness link inverted the concept it cited. Nothing is folded forward, because the only strand the digest supports here is the one it explicitly forbids applying to the crew.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
